scope: Proposition 5.5 (Uniform transfer density) of the manuscript “Determination of a metric and a unitary connection from one boundary patch” (preprints/Determination-of-a-metric-and-a-unitary-connection-from-one-boundary-patch-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8e1bdd3a90672348), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 37. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the fixed geometry as in Section 4, then choose p∗ sufficiently large, ε > 0 sufficiently small, and the radius amplitude R∗ > 0 sufficiently small that rδβ2 δ ≤ ε for 0 < δ ≤ 1. For all sufficiently small spatial dilations there is a constant C, independent of the dilation and δ, such that ∥χψδ∥L2(SγY ) ≤ C (5.34) whenever P |α|≤8 |∂αh| ≤ εrδ on Y . Here χ is the fixed cutoff from (4.9) and ψδ is the left-acting matrix density of Proposition 4.5.
